newsitem.title: UK: S&P assigns Sovereign Specialty Chemicals ratings.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns Sovereign Specialty Chemicals ratings.

text.p: LONDON, July 25 - Standard & Poor's today has assigned its single-'B'-plus corporate credit rating to Sovereign Specialty Chemicals, Inc. and its single-'B'-minus rating to the company's $110 million senior subordinated notes due 2007, to be sold under Rule 144A with registration rights.
In addition, Standard & Poor's has assigned its double-'B'-minus rating to Sovereign's $30 million secured revolving credit facility due 2004 and $30 million secured term loan maturing in 2004.
The ratings reflect a below average business profile and aggressive financial risk. Chicago-based Sovereign is a niche producer of industrial and commercial adhesives, sealants, and coatings.

The firm has been formed through the combination of several businesses over the last two years. Revenues exceed $200 million pro forma for the pending acquisition of the North American adhesive and sealants business of Laporte plc.

Sovereign is controlled by private investors, including First Chicago Equity Capital, and management. The adhesives, sealants, and coatings industry is fragmented, but is enjoying sustainable global growth of around 6% annually.

A number of large firms with substantially greater resources have significant market positions. However, management is well experienced in the industry, and the company has some good niche market positions and technology.
The firm is expected to pursue additional acquisitions to extend its position in core markets.
The rating on the $30 million term loan and the $30 million revolver is one notch higher than the corporate credit rating.
These credit facilities are equally secured by liens on all assets, including intellectual and real property, and the capital stock of the firm and its operating subsidiaries.

These lenders derive strength by having a secured position, and, based on Standard & Poor's simulated default scenario, it appears that a distressed enterprise value would be sufficient to fully cover these obligations.
Standard & Poor's relied on a preliminary credit agreement for its assessment of this facility and will finalize its review when a completed loan document is available.

Credit quality should be supported by good growth dynamics in markets served and the potential for some supplemental equity from the firm's sponsors should Sovereign consider relatively larger acquisition opportunities.
